title: The Odyssey in Art
note: Reproductions from Wikimedia Commons (public domain / CC0). 'src' links to the original file; 'display' is Commons' 1280px rendering used for playback. 'head' = [x,y] fractions (0-1) of Odysseus' head, set in the viewer.

scenes.title: The Wooden Horse is built
scenes.description: At Odysseus' prompting, Epeius builds a great hollow horse of wood with Athena's help. The Greeks feign departure, leaving the horse on the shore with the best warriors hidden inside.

scenes.title: The Horse is dragged into Troy
scenes.description: The Trojans haul the horse within their walls and debate its fate. Inside, Odysseus keeps the restless warriors silent, even clamping his hand over Anticlus' mouth when Helen circles the horse imitating their wives' voices.

scenes.title: The Greeks pour out of the Horse; Troy falls
scenes.description: At night the Achaeans climb down from the horse and sack the city. Demodocus will later sing how Odysseus, like Ares, went with Menelaus to the house of Deiphobus.

scenes.title: Clytemnestra and Aegisthus murder Agamemnon
scenes.description: Agamemnon returns home from Troy, only to be killed at a feast by Aegisthus and his wife Clytemnestra, together with Cassandra. His fate shadows the whole poem as the opposite of Odysseus' homecoming.

scenes.title: Raid on the Cicones at Ismarus
scenes.description: Blown from Troy to Ismarus, Odysseus and his men sack the city of the Cicones. Lingering to feast, they are attacked by Cicones from inland and lose six men from each ship.

scenes.title: The Lotus-Eaters
scenes.description: On the land of the Lotus-Eaters, scouts who taste the honey-sweet lotus forget all thought of home. Odysseus drags them weeping back to the ships and ties them beneath the benches.

scenes.title: In the cave of Polyphemus
scenes.description: Odysseus and twelve companions enter the cave of the Cyclops Polyphemus, son of Poseidon. The giant returns with his flocks, seals the entrance with a boulder and devours the men two at a time.

scenes.title: Odysseus gives the Cyclops wine
scenes.description: Odysseus offers Polyphemus the strong wine of Maron. The drunken giant asks his name: "Nobody," says Odysseus, and the Cyclops promises to eat Nobody last.

scenes.title: The blinding of Polyphemus
scenes.description: While the Cyclops sleeps, Odysseus and his men heat an olive-wood stake in the fire and drive it into his single eye. Polyphemus cries that Nobody is killing him, so his neighbours go away.

scenes.title: Escape beneath the rams
scenes.description: Each man is bound beneath a ram; Odysseus clings to the belly of the largest. The blind Cyclops feels the backs of his flock as they leave the cave, but not their undersides.

scenes.title: Odysseus taunts Polyphemus
scenes.description: From his ship Odysseus mocks the Cyclops and boasts his true name. Polyphemus hurls rocks at the ship and prays to his father Poseidon, who will make Odysseus' homecoming late and bitter.

scenes.title: Aeolus gives Odysseus the bag of winds
scenes.description: On his floating island, Aeolus, keeper of the winds, entertains Odysseus for a month and sends him off with all adverse winds tied up in an ox-hide bag and the West Wind to carry him home.

scenes.title: The crew opens the bag of winds
scenes.description: Within sight of Ithaca Odysseus falls asleep. Thinking the bag holds treasure, his men open it; the storm winds burst out and drive the fleet back to Aeolus, who now refuses to help.

scenes.title: The Laestrygonians destroy the fleet
scenes.description: The cannibal giants of Telepylus pelt the ships in the harbour with boulders and spear the men like fish. Only Odysseus' ship, moored outside, escapes.

scenes.title: Circe turns the companions into swine
scenes.description: On Aeaea, Eurylochus' scouting party is welcomed by the enchantress Circe, who gives them a potion and turns them into swine with a touch of her wand. Only Eurylochus escapes to tell Odysseus.

scenes.title: Hermes gives Odysseus the herb moly
scenes.description: On the way to Circe's house Odysseus meets Hermes in the guise of a young man, who gives him the herb moly to protect him from her drugs and tells him how to master her.

scenes.title: Odysseus threatens Circe with his sword
scenes.description: Circe's cup has no power over Odysseus. He draws his sword as if to kill her; she falls at his knees, recognises him and swears not to harm him.

scenes.title: A year with Circe
scenes.description: Circe restores the men to human form, younger and handsomer than before. They stay a year feasting in her hall, until the crew urge Odysseus to go; Circe tells him he must first visit the dead.

scenes.title: The sacrifice to the dead; Tiresias' prophecy
scenes.description: At the edge of the world Odysseus digs a pit and pours the blood of sheep, holding off the swarming shades with his sword until the blind seer Tiresias drinks and prophesies his homecoming.

scenes.title: Odysseus meets the shade of his mother
scenes.description: Among the dead Odysseus finds his mother Anticlea, who died of grief for him. Three times he tries to embrace her, and three times she slips through his arms like a shadow or a dream.

scenes.title: The heroes in the Underworld
scenes.description: Odysseus sees the famous women of old, then the shades of Agamemnon, Achilles and Ajax, who still will not speak to him. He glimpses Minos, Orion, Tityus, Tantalus, Sisyphus and Heracles before fear drives him back to the ship.

scenes.title: The Sirens
scenes.description: Warned by Circe, Odysseus stops his men's ears with wax and has himself bound to the mast so that he alone may hear the Sirens' song. He begs to be released; they row on.

scenes.title: Between Scylla and Charybdis
scenes.description: Steering past the whirlpool Charybdis, the ship passes too near the six-headed monster Scylla, who snatches six of the crew from the deck.

scenes.title: The companions slaughter the cattle of the Sun
scenes.description: Becalmed on Thrinacia and starving, the men disobey the warnings and kill the sacred cattle of Helios while Odysseus sleeps. The hides crawl and the meat lows on the spits.

scenes.title: Zeus destroys the ship
scenes.description: At Helios' demand Zeus strikes the ship with a thunderbolt. All the crew drown; Odysseus, clinging to the keel and mast, is swept back past Charybdis and drifts nine days to Calypso's island.

scenes.title: With Calypso on Ogygia
scenes.description: For seven years the nymph Calypso keeps Odysseus in her cave, wishing to make him immortal. By day he sits on the shore weeping and gazing out over the sea toward home.

scenes.title: Menelaus wrestles Proteus
scenes.description: Becalmed on Pharos off Egypt on his own way home, Menelaus, disguised under sealskins, seizes the shape-shifting Old Man of the Sea, Proteus, and holds him until he reveals the way home and the fates of the other Greeks.

scenes.title: Orestes avenges his father
scenes.description: In the eighth year after Agamemnon's death, Orestes returns from exile and kills Aegisthus (and Clytemnestra). Athena holds him up to Telemachus as an example.

scenes.title: Penelope's web
scenes.description: Penelope promises the suitors she will choose a husband when she finishes weaving a shroud for Laertes. For three years she weaves by day and unravels the work by night, until a maid betrays her.

scenes.title: Penelope and the suitors
scenes.description: More than a hundred suitors occupy Odysseus' house, feasting on his herds and pressing Penelope to marry one of them.

scenes.title: The council of the gods
scenes.description: While Poseidon is away among the Ethiopians, Athena pleads with Zeus on Olympus for Odysseus, held captive by Calypso. Zeus agrees that he shall return home.

scenes.title: Athena, as Mentes, visits Telemachus
scenes.description: Disguised as Mentes, a guest-friend of his father, Athena visits young Telemachus amid the riotous suitors and urges him to seek news of Odysseus.

scenes.title: Phemius sings; Penelope descends
scenes.description: The bard Phemius sings to the suitors of the Greeks' bitter return from Troy. Penelope comes down from her chamber in tears and asks him to sing something else; Telemachus sends her back upstairs.

scenes.title: Telemachus sails with Athena as Mentor
scenes.description: After a failed assembly of the Ithacans, Athena, now in the guise of old Mentor, finds Telemachus a ship and sails with him by night in search of news of his father.

scenes.title: Telemachus at Nestor's in Pylos
scenes.description: At sandy Pylos Telemachus finds old Nestor sacrificing to Poseidon on the shore. Nestor tells of the homecomings from Troy and the murder of Agamemnon, and sends him on to Sparta with his son Peisistratus.

scenes.title: Telemachus with Menelaus and Helen in Sparta
scenes.description: In the shining palace of Menelaus, Helen recognises Telemachus by his likeness to Odysseus, drugs the wine against sorrow and tells stories of his father at Troy.

scenes.title: Penelope's grief and dream
scenes.description: Penelope learns that Telemachus has sailed and that the suitors plan to ambush him. Weeping, she falls asleep, and Athena sends her a dream in the shape of her sister Iphthime to comfort her.

scenes.title: Hermes brings Zeus' command to Calypso
scenes.description: Hermes flies over the sea to Calypso's cave, filled with the scent of cedar fire, and tells her that Zeus commands her to let Odysseus go. She protests, but obeys.

scenes.title: Calypso lets Odysseus go; the raft
scenes.description: Calypso finds Odysseus weeping on the shore and promises to help him leave. She gives him tools; he fells trees and builds a raft in four days, and she sends him off with provisions and a fair wind.

scenes.title: Poseidon's storm; Leucothea's veil
scenes.description: Poseidon sees Odysseus on the sea and smashes his raft with a storm. The sea goddess Ino Leucothea gives him her veil to keep him afloat, and after two days he crawls ashore on Scheria and sleeps under the leaves.

scenes.title: Nausicaa and her maidens at the river
scenes.description: Prompted by Athena in a dream, the Phaeacian princess Nausicaa drives to the river with her maids to wash clothes. Afterwards they play ball on the shore; the ball falls in the water and their cries wake Odysseus.

scenes.title: Odysseus appears before Nausicaa
scenes.description: Naked and caked with brine, Odysseus emerges from the thicket holding a leafy branch before him. The maids flee; only Nausicaa stands her ground as he makes his supplication.

scenes.title: Nausicaa gives Odysseus clothes
scenes.description: Nausicaa gives the stranger clothing and oil. He bathes in the river and Athena makes him tall and radiant; Nausicaa, admiring him, tells him how to reach the palace and win her mother's favour.

scenes.title: Odysseus in the palace of Alcinous and Arete
scenes.description: Wrapped in a mist by Athena, Odysseus enters the palace of King Alcinous and clasps the knees of Queen Arete in supplication. The Phaeacians receive him with feasting and games.

scenes.title: Demodocus' song: Ares and Aphrodite caught by Hephaestus
scenes.description: The bard Demodocus sings how Hephaestus caught his wife Aphrodite in bed with Ares in an invisible net of chains, and summoned the gods, who burst into unquenchable laughter.

scenes.title: Odysseus weeps at Demodocus' song
scenes.description: When the blind bard Demodocus sings of the quarrel at Troy and of the Wooden Horse, Odysseus hides his face in his cloak and weeps. Alcinous asks who he is, and Odysseus begins the tale of his wanderings.

scenes.title: The Phaeacians carry Odysseus to Ithaca
scenes.description: The Phaeacians convey Odysseus home overnight on their magical ship and set him down, still sleeping, on the shore of Ithaca with his treasures beside him.

scenes.title: Poseidon turns the Phaeacian ship to stone
scenes.description: As the Phaeacian ship returns to harbour, Poseidon strikes it with the flat of his hand and turns it to stone in sight of the city.

scenes.title: Athena meets Odysseus on Ithaca
scenes.description: Odysseus wakes not knowing his own land. Athena, first as a young shepherd, then in her own form, reveals Ithaca, helps him hide his treasure in a cave of the nymphs, and disguises him as an old beggar.

scenes.title: Odysseus in the hut of Eumaeus
scenes.description: The disguised Odysseus is welcomed by the loyal swineherd Eumaeus, who saves him from the dogs, shares his meal and laments his lost master.

scenes.title: Telemachus returns to Ithaca
scenes.description: Athena appears to Telemachus in Sparta and urges him home. He leaves with gifts from Menelaus and Helen, takes the seer Theoclymenus aboard at Pylos and evades the suitors' ambush.

scenes.title: Odysseus reveals himself to Telemachus
scenes.description: In Eumaeus' hut Athena restores Odysseus' true form. He reveals himself to his son; they embrace and weep, then plot the suitors' destruction.

scenes.title: The dog Argos recognises his master
scenes.description: Lying neglected on a dung heap, the old dog Argos recognises Odysseus after twenty years. He wags his tail and drops his ears, and dies.

scenes.title: The beggar in his own hall
scenes.description: Odysseus begs from the suitors in his own house. Antinous hits him with a footstool, and the suitors set him to box the beggar Irus, whom he knocks down with one blow.

scenes.title: Penelope talks with the beggar
scenes.description: At night Penelope questions the stranger by the fire. He tells her he has news of Odysseus; she tells him of her web, of her dream of the eagle and the geese, and of the contest of the bow.

scenes.title: Eurycleia recognises the scar
scenes.description: The old nurse Eurycleia washes the beggar's feet and recognises the scar left by a boar's tusk in his youth. She drops his foot in the basin; Odysseus grips her throat and swears her to silence.

scenes.title: Penelope brings the bow; the contest
scenes.description: Penelope fetches the great bow of Odysseus and sets the suitors the contest: whoever can string it and shoot through twelve axe-heads will win her. None of them can bend it.

scenes.title: Odysseus strings the bow
scenes.description: The beggar asks to try. He strings the bow as easily as a musician strings a lyre, plucks the string, which sings like a swallow, and shoots through all twelve axes.

scenes.title: The slaughter of the suitors
scenes.description: Odysseus throws off his rags and shoots Antinous through the throat. With Telemachus, Eumaeus and the cowherd Philoetius, and with Athena's aegis terrifying the suitors, he kills them all.

scenes.title: Penelope and Odysseus reunited
scenes.description: Eurycleia wakes Penelope with the news, but she doubts. She tests the stranger with the secret of their bed built round an olive tree; when he describes it she runs to embrace him, and Athena holds back the dawn.

scenes.title: Hermes leads the suitors' souls to Hades
scenes.description: Hermes, with his golden wand, drives the gibbering souls of the suitors down to the asphodel meadow, where the shade of Agamemnon praises the faithfulness of Penelope.

scenes.title: Odysseus and Laertes
scenes.description: Odysseus finds his old father Laertes digging in his orchard and, after testing him, reveals himself by his scar and by the trees Laertes once gave him as a boy.

scenes.title: Athena makes peace in Ithaca
scenes.description: The suitors' kinsmen come for revenge. After Laertes kills Eupeithes, Athena, at Zeus' command, stops the fighting and establishes peace between Odysseus and the people of Ithaca.

images.description: This plaque is among the earliest examples of the technique of enamel on copper used during the Renaissance to depict secular scenes.
